Samir Patel: Hey folks — working on my first PR here. It’s a tiny docs tweak + a small config change for logging levels. Quick questions: which branch should I target for this (main vs release/*)? Do we prefer squashed commits for small changes? And is there a preferred commit message format I should use? Thanks!

Tasha Nguyen: For that combo (docs + non-breaking config), main is the right target. release/* is only for urgent hotfixes we need to ship in the next patch.

Tasha Nguyen: We usually squash for small changes to keep history tidy, unless the PR contains distinct logical steps you want to preserve. Size threshold is fuzzy — if it’s < ~5 commits and tightly related, squash. :+1:

Tasha Nguyen: Commit message format we prefer: <area>(<scope>): <short summary>

Example:
```
runtime(kv-cache): lower log level for debug noise

Reduce noise from repeated cache hits; no behavior changes.
```

Mike Chen: Also note we have pre-commit hooks and CI expectations for PRs. Before opening, run:
```
pre-commit run --all-files
make test-local  # runs lint + a subset of unit tests fast
```
If CI fails, address the errors locally first — faster to iterate.

Olivia Rivera: For reviewers, check CODEOWNERS to see who’s auto-assigned. For runtime-ish bits ping @eng-runtime, for docs ping @devex. Add labels: `type/docs` and `size/XS` (or `size/S` if slightly bigger).

Olivia Rivera: Also fill the PR template top section and add a one-line QA step (e.g., "ran make test-local, no regressions"). That speeds approval.

ci-bot: CI status: queued -> running (build/ci: unit-tests)

Samir Patel: Thanks! One more: branch name convention?

Mike Chen: We usually use: `<yourname>/pr/<short-summary>` or `<yourname>/fix/<short-summary>` for tiny fixes. Example: `samir/pr/kv-log-level`

Mike Chen: If you need to squash locally:
```
git rebase -i HEAD~N  # mark commits as squash
git push --force-with-lease origin <branch>
```

Tasha Nguyen: Review SLAs: aim for 24-48h turnaround. If you need faster, add `review/fast` label and ping an oncall reviewer in the PR thread.

Samir Patel: Awesome — this is super helpful. I’ll target main, squash, follow the commit format, run pre-commit and tests, and request reviewers from CODEOWNERS. Thanks everyone! :raised_hands:
